locations.quote: Integrating large language models (LLMs) to assist supervisors with non-content-related feedback could improve the thesis writing process. As Figure 1 illustrates, an LLM-powered Reviewer works alongside the supervisor, evaluating the thesis against the research group's writing guidelines and generating automatic formative feedback [NM06]. This Reviewer covers exactly the repetitive, non-content-related layer of feedback that currently drains supervisors, freeing them to focus on specific content and on discussions with their students, which is key in mentoring environments [BBE10, NM06]. **The quality of feedback improves as supervisors have more time to engage deeply with the thesis, leading to better outcomes overall. Additionally, supervisors can provide feedback faster, making the process more scalable.**

locations.quote: Better and faster feedback has significant advantages for students as well. When feedback arrives sooner, students can act on it while the writing process is still fresh in their minds. **The student brings both knowledge, comprising theoretical and practical domain expertise, and beliefs about how to approach the task and how to work and write scientifically, which include the student's personal interpretation of the writing guidelines. Drawing on this knowledge and these beliefs, the student writes the thesis. Through self-regulated learning, the student engages with the Reviewer's feedback, reflecting on it independently or discussing it with the supervisor, and uses it to improve their knowledge, beliefs, and broader strategy for proceeding with the work [NM06]. Because the feedback tool is powered by LLMs, students can obtain instant formative feedback at any point during the writing process.**
